title: Article 317 — Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission

content.overview: Article 317 provides that the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission shall only be removed from office by order of the President on the ground of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on reference by the President, has reported that the Chairman or member ought on any such ground to be removed. The President may suspend the Chairman/member in respect of whom a reference has been made to the Supreme Court until the President has passed orders on receipt of the report. The President may also remove on specified grounds including insolvency, paid employment outside the duties of office, or infirmity of mind or body.
content.glance: Removal of PSC Chairman/member: by President on misbehaviour after SC inquiry and report; or on insolvency, outside paid employment, or infirmity. Suspension pending SC reference.
content.study:
Article 317 removal and suspension:
1. Misbehaviour: President removes only after reference to the Supreme Court and SC report that the person ought to be removed on that ground.
2. Suspension: President may suspend pending the SC reference/report.
3. Other grounds (President may remove): insolvency; engaging during term in paid employment outside the duties of office; infirmity of mind or body.

Examination: SC inquiry for misbehaviour; other listed grounds; suspension pending reference; protects PSC independence.

sections.heading: Removal pathways
sections.body:
1. Misbehaviour: President’s order only after SC inquiry on reference and adverse report.
2. Suspension pending SC reference.
3. Other grounds: insolvency; paid outside employment; infirmity of mind or body.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How may a member of a Public Service Commission be removed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 317, the Chairman or any other member of a Public Service Commission shall only be removed from office by order of the President on the ground of misbehaviour after the Supreme Court, on reference by the President, has reported that the person ought to be removed on that ground. The President may suspend the person pending the reference. The President may also remove a Chairman or member who is adjudged insolvent, engages during his term in paid employment outside the duties of his office, or is unfit to continue by reason of infirmity of mind or body.

examTips: Misbehaviour → SC inquiry then President removes; also insolvency/employment/infirmity.

keyTakeaways: Art 317: removal and suspension of PSC members — SC role on misbehaviour.
